problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $4$ | $-1$ | $2$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$ Do not round the answer.

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=0$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(0)g(0)-f(0){g}^{′}(0)}{(g(0))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)(4)-(\frac{1}{2})(2)}{{4}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-4-1}{16} \\  & =-\frac{5}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
